idiom_name: object literal or closure handed to the SUT as the collaborator (recording state in the test closure)
implementation_notes: JavaScript has no interfaces, so any object with the right shape is the collaborator: the test passes an object literal whose method records into an array in the test's closure -- the Self Shunt reduced to its minimum, since there is no declaration to implement. When the SUT calls a single function, an arrow function is passed directly; when call counting, argument capture or a canned implementation is needed, jest.fn() supplies those recording mechanisms and replaces the hand-written shunt as the natural escalation. The literal form stays justified for multi-method collaborator contracts (listener objects, adapters) where the recorder should sit next to the assertions rather than inside a framework mock.
pitfalls: Callbacks delivered asynchronously can fire after the test body or after afterEach tore the fixture down; await the SUT's completion signal or unsubscribe before asserting.
Module-level recording state leaks between tests running in the same process; keep the array inside the test closure or reset it in beforeEach.
Passing a bare function where the SUT calls a method on the collaborator loses the receiver (this) and throws; check whether the seam expects a function or an object with methods.
